The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click SmallBusinessProfitPlan.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on logging entries, profit, tax money and backups.
  4. Follow the five steps on the Dashboard: your name and currency, your sales channels, your monthly targets, your first entries, and a backup.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data on the Dashboard or in Settings & backup. Juniper Studio, a fictional design studio with an Etsy shop, fills every screen with ten months of sales, costs, invoices and trips, in a separate session. Return to my books brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

Every dollar in, every dollar out.

The Dashboard answers the monthly question: what came in, what went out, what the business kept, and what you owe.

WordWhat it means
RevenueMoney received from sales and clients. An invoice counts on the day it’s paid.
Net profitRevenue − cost of goods − running costs. What the business actually made.
Transfers & drawsMoney you move to savings or pay yourself. Not an expense, so it doesn’t lower profit.
Net cash flowRevenue − expenses − transfers: what’s left in the business account.

Each week

Log it, or import it.

Transactions → Add transaction takes seconds: date, amount, category and channel. Or Import CSV once a month.

Your bank’s CSV

Download it from online banking and drop it in. You check every line before it’s added; lines you imported before are skipped, and the categories you pick are remembered.

Platform statements

Etsy, Shopify, PayPal and Stripe downloads are recognized: sales, refunds, fees and ads land on their own lines, and payouts to your bank aren’t counted twice.

Invoices

Who still owes you.

Invoices → Add invoice for each bill you send. When the money arrives, Mark paid and it becomes revenue on that day.

How late is the money?Open invoices grouped by days past due, so the oldest are chased first.
ReminderA friendly payment reminder, filled in from the invoice, ready to copy into an email.
Undo paidMarked one paid by mistake? One click puts it back, and the revenue entry goes too.

Tax money

Set tax aside as you go.

Quarterly tax works out what you should have put aside by each due date, at the rate you set (25% to start), and whether your pot covers it.

Log a set-aside

Each time you move money to your tax savings, log it. The pot and “ahead by” update straight away.

Change rate

Ask your tax pro what share of profit to keep back, and set it here. The due dates are the usual US estimated-tax dates.

These are worksheets, not tax advice: rules differ by country and change every year.

Tax time

Schedule C, ready for your accountant.

Every category sits on its Schedule C line, so the year’s summary builds itself. Print it or download the Summary CSV.

Mileage log

Log a trip: date, purpose, route and miles. The value is worked out at your rate (set it in Settings), and Export year CSV gives your accountant the list.

Profit & loss

Month, quarter, year to date, full year or your own dates, for the whole business or one channel. Print statement or Download CSV.

Read this one

Keeping your books safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every transaction, invoice, trip, target, category and setting. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
Profit looks too lowA transfer to savings or an owner’s draw may be filed as an expense. Change its category to a transfer.
A sale shows twiceA platform’s deposit in your bank was filed as revenue as well as its statement. Change the deposit’s category to the payout transfer; imports do this for Etsy, Shopify, PayPal and Stripe.
An invoice isn’t in revenueInvoices count when they’re marked paid. Open Invoices → Mark paid.
My PDF statement won’t importOnly CSV downloads can be read. Look for “Export” or “Download CSV” in online banking.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
